revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Choosing a Time-Capsule Box
revealWordProblem.text: Your class is choosing a box for the time capsule. The store sells three rectangular-prism boxes: a Small box that is 2 ft × 1 ft × 1 ft, a Medium box that is 2 ft × 1.5 ft × 1 ft, and a Large box that is 2 ft × 2 ft × 1.5 ft. Compute the volume of each box in cubic feet. Which box should the class buy if they need to fit at least 5 cubic feet of items? Explain how you decided.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Small: V = 2 × 1 × 1 = 2 ft³. Medium: V = 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 ft³. Large: V = 2 × 2 × 1.5 = 6 ft³. The class should buy the Large box because only its volume, 6 ft³, is at least 5 ft³.

launch.narrative: This is your support small group for Lesson 5.10. We're going to slow this down and build it together, one step at a time. You can ask a question any time — that's what this group is for.
launch.contextImage: Students gathered around a rectangular box time capsule with items to place inside
noticePrompts: What are the three measurements of the time capsule?
What does volume measure — length, area, or space inside?
How is volume different from area?
wonderPrompts: What if we made the capsule taller but narrower — would the volume change?
What units do we use for volume versus area?

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How do we find volume when an edge is a fraction?
conceptIntro.intro: Volume is the space inside a rectangular prism. The rule V = length × width × height stays the same even when one edge is a fraction or decimal. You can also use volume = base area × height. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: A fractional edge does not change the rule: still multiply length × width × height.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My capsule is 2 ft long, 1.5 ft wide, and 1 ft tall. I write V = length × width × height.
I put in the numbers: V = 2 × 1.5 × 1.
So the volume is 3 ft³. A fractional edge like 1.5 did not change my steps at all.
linesEs: Mi cápsula mide 2 pies de largo, 1.5 pies de ancho y 1 pie de alto. Escribo V = largo × ancho × alto.
Entonces el volumen es 3 pies³. Una arista fraccionaria como 1.5 no cambió mis pasos para nada.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now try a box that is 4 long, 2 wide, and 0.5 tall. What formula do we use?
Put in the numbers: V = 4 × 2 × 0.5. What is 4 × 2?
We got 8. Now multiply 8 × 0.5 (that means half of 8). What is the volume?
Yes, V = 4 cubic units. The decimal edge just made the answer a little smaller.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "My first step is ___ , because the problem asks for ___ ."
linesEs: Ahora prueba con una caja de 4 de largo, 2 de ancho y 0.5 de alto. ¿Qué fórmula usamos?
Nos dio 8. Ahora multiplica 8 × 0.5 (eso significa la mitad de 8). ¿Cuál es el volumen?
Sí, V = 4 unidades cúbicas. La arista decimal solo hizo la respuesta un poco más pequeña.
Marco de oración — dilo conmigo: «Mi primer paso es ___ , porque el problema pide ___ .»

youDo.title: Now you try — with support

Remember the key idea: A fractional edge does not change the rule: still multiply length × width × height..

Recuerda la idea clave: Una arista fraccionaria no cambia la regla: sigue multiplicando largo × ancho × alto.

conceptIntro.headingEs: Construyámoslo juntos — ¿Cómo hallamos el volumen cuando una arista es una fracción?
conceptIntro.introEs: El volumen es el espacio dentro de un prisma rectangular. La regla V = largo × ancho × alto sigue siendo la misma incluso cuando una arista es una fracción o un decimal. También puedes usar volumen = área de la base × altura. Veremos un ejemplo resuelto, haremos uno juntos y luego harás algunos con pistas disponibles cuando las necesites.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Una arista fraccionaria no cambia la regla: sigue multiplicando largo × ancho × alto.

discourse.sentenceFrame: Capsules A and B both have V = ___ because ___ × ___ × ___ = ___ × ___ × ___. I'd choose ___ because ___.

approaching.stem: What is the volume of a rectangular prism with l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in?
approaching.explanation: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60 cubic inches.
choiceFeedback: Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
Check the units. Area is square units (²), volume is cubic units (³).
Not quite. V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = ___ cubic inches.
hints: Spot the three edges: l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in. Volume fills the whole box, so all three matter.
Use V = l × w × h and remember the answer needs cubic units (in³), not square units.
Multiply 4 × 3 = 12 for the base, then multiply that result by the height, 5 inches.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el volumen de un prisma rectangular con l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in?
approaching.explanationEs: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60 pulgadas cúbicas.
hintsEs: Identifica las tres aristas: l = 4 pulg, a = 3 pulg, h = 5 pulg. El volumen llena toda la caja, así que las tres importan.
Usa V = l × a × h y recuerda que la respuesta necesita unidades cúbicas (pulg³), no cuadradas.
Multiplica 4 × 3 = 12 para la base y luego multiplica ese resultado por la altura, 5 pulgadas.

approaching.stem: A box has a volume of 36 cm³. Its length is 6 cm and width is 3 cm. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: That number is the length given in the problem — divide volume by the full base area to find height.
That's the width from the problem, not the height — divide the volume by length × width instead.
Check your division — find the full base area (length × width) before dividing into the volume.
hints: You're given the volume (36 cm³) plus two edges (6 cm and 3 cm). The height is what's missing.
Work backward: divide the volume by the base area (length × width) to uncover the height.
Find the base area first: 6 × 3 = 18 cm². Then ask what number times 18 gives 36.
approaching.stemEs: Una caja tiene un volumen de 36 cm³. Su longitud es 6 cm y su ancho es 3 cm. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Te dan el volumen (36 cm³) más dos aristas (6 cm y 3 cm). Lo que falta es la altura.
Trabaja al revés: divide el volumen entre el área de la base (largo × ancho) para descubrir la altura.
Halla primero el área de la base: 6 × 3 = 18 cm². Luego pregunta qué número por 18 da 36.

approaching.stem: How is volume different from area?
choices: Volume measures 3D space (cubic units); area measures 2D surface (square units)
Volume uses square units; area uses cubic units
Volume only applies to cubes; area applies to all shapes
approaching.explanation: Volume measures the space inside a 3D shape (cubic units like in³). Area measures a flat 2D surface (square units like in²).
choiceFeedback: The units are swapped here — think about which measurement fills 3D space and which covers a flat surface.
Volume isn't just for cubes — it applies to any 3D shape, like prisms and pyramids too.
These two measurements are different — one covers a flat surface, and one fills a 3D space.
hints: Think dimensions: area covers a flat 2D surface, while volume fills a 3D space.
Match each measurement to its unit: flat surfaces get square units (²), filled space gets cubic units (³).
Picture a rug (flat) versus a fish tank (filled). Decide which is area and which is volume, then check each choice.
approaching.stemEs: ¿En qué se diferencia el volumen del área?
approaching.explanationEs: El volumen mide el espacio dentro de una figura de tres dimensiones (unidades cúbicas como in³). El área mide una superficie plana de dos dimensiones (unidades cuadradas como in²).
choicesEs: El volumen mide el espacio en 3D (unidades cúbicas); el área mide una superficie en 2D (unidades cuadradas)
El volumen usa unidades cuadradas; el área usa unidades cúbicas
El volumen solo aplica a los cubos; el área aplica a todas las figuras
hintsEs: Piensa en dimensiones: el área cubre una superficie plana 2D, mientras que el volumen llena un espacio 3D.
Une cada medida con su unidad: las superficies planas llevan unidades cuadradas (²) y el espacio lleno lleva unidades cúbicas (³).
Imagina una alfombra (plana) frente a una pecera (llena). Decide cuál es área y cuál es volumen, y luego revisa cada opción.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: A box is 5 in long, 4 in wide, and 2 in tall.
workedExample.workEs: Una caja mide 5 pulg de largo, 4 pulg de ancho y 2 pulg de alto.

approaching.correctWork: The student added the dimensions instead of multiplying. Volume means multiply: V = 5 × 4 × 2 = 20 × 2 = 40 cubic in.
hints: Check Step 3: should you add the dimensions or multiply them?
Volume is length × width × height. Multiply: 5 × 4 × 2 = 40 cubic in, not 11.
approaching.explanation: The Calculate step added the three dimensions instead of multiplying them. Volume counts the cubes that fill the box, so the edges multiply: V = 5 × 4 × 2 = 20 × 2 = 40 cubic in, not 11.
approaching.explanationEs: En el paso de calcular se sumaron las tres dimensiones en lugar de multiplicarlas. El volumen cuenta los cubos que llenan la caja, así que los lados se multiplican: V = 5 × 4 × 2 = 20 × 2 = 40 pulgadas cúbicas, no 11.
approaching.correctWorkEs: El estudiante sumó las dimensiones en lugar de multiplicarlas. Volumen significa multiplicar: V = 5 × 4 × 2 = 20 × 2 = 40 pulg cúbicas.
hintsEs: Revisa el Paso 3: ¿debes sumar las dimensiones o multiplicarlas?
El volumen es largo × ancho × alto. Multiplica: 5 × 4 × 2 = 40 pulgadas cúbicas, no 11.

approaching.instructions: Find the volume of each rectangular prism.
approaching.hint: Use the formula V = length × width × height for each row.
hints: Each row lists a length, width, and height. The blank Volume cell needs a number with cubic units.
For every row use V = l × w × h: multiply the first two numbers, then multiply by the third.
Row 1: multiply 8 × 5 = 40 first, then multiply by the height, 2. Include in³ in your answer.
approaching.explanation: Volume counts the unit cubes that fill a prism, and V = length × width × height finds that count: 8 × 5 × 2 = 80 in³, 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 cm³, and 10 × 3 × 6 = 180 ft³. Because three lengths are multiplied, the units come out cubic.
approaching.explanationEs: El volumen cuenta los cubos unitarios que llenan un prisma, y V = largo × ancho × altura encuentra esa cantidad: 8 × 5 × 2 = 80 in³, 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 cm³ y 10 × 3 × 6 = 180 ft³. Como se multiplican tres longitudes, las unidades quedan cúbicas.
approaching.instructionsEs: Encuentra el volumen de cada prisma rectangular.
hintsEs: Cada fila indica un largo, un ancho y una altura. La celda vacía de Volumen necesita un número con unidades cúbicas.
Para cada fila usa V = l × a × h: multiplica los dos primeros números y luego multiplica por el tercero.
Fila 1: multiplica 8 × 5 = 40 primero y luego multiplica por la altura, 2. Incluye pulg³ en tu respuesta.

approaching.label: Sort these boxes from SMALLEST volume to LARGEST volume.
approaching.hint: Think about the order of steps in solving a volume problem.
hints: Each card gives a box's three measurements. Multiply all three to get its volume, then sort by that total.
Ignore how long or tall each box looks — compare only the volume numbers, smallest to largest.
Scan for the smallest total and drag that card first, then keep choosing the next smallest.
approaching.explanation: Each card already shows its product, so ordering them is just comparing totals: 20, then 60, then 64, then 84, then 90. A box with one long edge is not automatically bigger — 10 × 2 × 3 = 60 holds less than the cube 4 × 4 × 4 = 64.
approaching.explanationEs: Cada tarjeta ya muestra su producto, así que ordenarlas es solo comparar totales: 20, luego 60, luego 64, luego 84 y luego 90. Una caja con un lado largo no es automáticamente más grande: 10 × 2 × 3 = 60 guarda menos que el cubo 4 × 4 × 4 = 64.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta muestra su volumen después del signo igual, como 2 × 2 × 5 = 20. Clasifica por esos totales.
Ignora qué tan larga o alta se ve cada caja: compara solo los números de volumen, de menor a mayor.
Busca el total más pequeño y arrastra esa tarjeta primero; luego sigue eligiendo el siguiente más pequeño.

onLevel.stem: Two boxes: Box A is 10 × 5 × 4 inches. Box B is 8 × 6 × 5 inches. Which has more volume and by how much?
onLevel.explanation: Box A: 10 × 5 × 4 = 200 in³. Box B: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Box B is bigger by 40 in³.
choiceFeedback: Recheck which box's volume is larger — recalculate both totals before comparing.
You picked the right box, but recheck the subtraction to find the exact difference.
These two volumes aren't equal — calculate each box's volume and compare the totals.
hints: This asks two things: which box holds more AND by how many cubic inches — so find both volumes first.
Compute each volume with V = l × w × h, then subtract the smaller total from the larger.
Box A: 10 × 5 = 50, then × 4. Box B: 8 × 6 = 48, then × 5. Compare the two totals.
onLevel.stemEs: Dos cajas: la caja A mide 10 × 5 × 4 pulgadas. La caja B mide 8 × 6 × 5 pulgadas. ¿Cuál tiene más volumen y por cuánto?
onLevel.explanationEs: Caja A: 10 × 5 × 4 = 200 in³. Caja B: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. La caja B es mayor por 40 in³.
hintsEs: Esto pregunta dos cosas: cuál caja guarda más Y por cuántas pulgadas cúbicas, así que halla primero ambos volúmenes.
Calcula cada volumen con V = l × a × h y luego resta el total menor del mayor.
Caja A: 10 × 5 = 50 y luego × 4. Caja B: 8 × 6 = 48 y luego × 5. Compara los dos totales.

onLevel.stem: What is the volume of a prism with edge lengths 1/2 m, 3 m, and 4 m?
choiceFeedback: Adding the three edge lengths together won't give volume — multiply them instead.
Check the fractional edge — make sure you multiply by 1/2, not treat it as a whole number.
That's just one edge length — volume needs all three dimensions multiplied together.
hints: One edge is a fraction: 1/2 m. The other edges are 3 m and 4 m. The formula works the same with fractions.
Multiply all three edges: V = 1/2 × 3 × 4. Multiplying by 1/2 is the same as dividing by 2.
Multiply the whole numbers first: 3 × 4 = 12. Then take half of that result.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el volumen de un prisma con longitudes de arista de 1/2 m, 3 m y 4 m?
hintsEs: Una arista es una fracción: 1/2 m. Las otras aristas son 3 m y 4 m. La fórmula funciona igual con fracciones.
Multiplica las tres aristas: V = 1/2 × 3 × 4. Multiplicar por 1/2 es lo mismo que dividir entre 2.
Multiplica primero los números enteros: 3 × 4 = 12. Luego saca la mitad de ese resultado.

onLevel.stem: A cube has an edge length of 5 cm. What is its volume?
onLevel.explanation: A cube's volume is edge³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cm³.
choiceFeedback: Adding the edge three times won't give volume — multiply the edge by itself three times instead.
You squared the edge but forgot to multiply by it once more — a cube's volume needs edge × edge × edge.
Check your last multiplication — multiply the squared edge by the same edge length again.
hints: A cube's edges are all equal, so its length, width, and height are each 5 cm.
Use V = edge × edge × edge — multiply 5 by itself three times, not 5 × 3.
Start with 5 × 5 = 25, then multiply that result by 5 one more time.
onLevel.stemEs: Un cubo tiene una longitud de arista de 5 cm. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
onLevel.explanationEs: El volumen de un cubo es arista³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cm³.
hintsEs: Las aristas de un cubo son todas iguales, así que su largo, ancho y altura son 5 cm cada uno.
Usa V = arista × arista × arista: multiplica 5 por sí mismo tres veces, no 5 × 3.
Empieza con 5 × 5 = 25 y luego multiplica ese resultado por 5 una vez más.

onLevel.stem: A time-capsule box measures 6 in long, 4 in wide, and 3 in tall. What is its volume?
onLevel.explanation: V = length × width × height = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic in. Volume uses cubic units.
choiceFeedback: Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
You multiplied two dimensions but forgot the third — include length, width, AND height.
Check the units — this fills 3D space, so it needs cubic units, not square units.
onLevel.stemEs: Una caja para una cápsula del tiempo mide 6 in de largo, 4 in de ancho y 3 in de alto. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
onLevel.explanationEs: V = largo × ancho × alto = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 pulgadas cúbicas. El volumen usa unidades cúbicas.
hints: Volume measures the space inside a solid, and it is always labeled in cubic units.
Use V = length × width × height: multiply two of the dimensions first, then multiply by the third.
Start with 6 × 4 = 24. Now multiply that result by the height of 3.
hintsEs: El volumen mide el espacio dentro de un cuerpo y siempre se escribe en unidades cúbicas.
Usa V = largo × ancho × alto: multiplica primero dos de las dimensiones y luego multiplica por la tercera.
Empieza con 6 × 4 = 24. Ahora multiplica ese resultado por la altura de 3.

onLevel.stem: Two storage boxes are ready to pack. Box A is 5 × 5 × 2 inches and Box B is 4 × 4 × 3 inches. Which box holds more?
choices: Box A, because 50 cubic in is more than 48 cubic in
Box B, because 48 cubic in is more than 50 cubic in
Box B, because it is taller
onLevel.explanation: Box A: 5 × 5 × 2 = 50 cubic in. Box B: 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 cubic in. 50 > 48, so Box A holds more.
choiceFeedback: Compare the two volume numbers again — which one is actually larger?
The two boxes have different volumes — calculate each one and compare the totals.
Height alone doesn't decide which holds more — compare the full volumes instead.
onLevel.stemEs: Hay dos cajas de almacenamiento listas para empacar. La caja A mide 5 × 5 × 2 pulgadas y la caja B mide 4 × 4 × 3 pulgadas. ¿Cuál caja guarda más?
onLevel.explanationEs: Caja A: 5 × 5 × 2 = 50 pulgadas cúbicas. Caja B: 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 pulgadas cúbicas. 50 > 48, así que la caja A guarda más.
hints: How much a box holds is its volume, not its height or its widest side.
Find the volume of each box separately with V = l × w × h, then compare the two numbers.
For Box A, 5 × 5 = 25, then multiply by 2. Do the same kind of work for Box B before comparing.
hintsEs: Lo que cabe en una caja es su volumen, no su altura ni su lado más ancho.
Halla el volumen de cada caja por separado con V = l × w × h y luego compara los dos números.
Para la caja A, 5 × 5 = 25 y luego multiplica por 2. Haz el mismo trabajo con la caja B antes de comparar.
choicesEs: La caja A, porque 50 pulgadas cúbicas es más que 48 pulgadas cúbicas
La caja B, porque 48 pulgadas cúbicas es más que 50 pulgadas cúbicas
La caja B, porque es más alta

onLevel.stem: A keepsake box is 4 in long, 3 in wide, and 1½ in tall. What is its volume?
onLevel.explanation: V = 4 × 3 × 1.5 = 12 × 1.5 = 18 cubic in. A fractional edge does not change the steps.
choiceFeedback: Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
You found the base area but forgot to multiply by the height for volume.
Double check the height value — using the wrong height changes your answer too much.
onLevel.stemEs: Una caja de recuerdos mide 4 in de largo, 3 in de ancho y 1½ in de alto. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
onLevel.explanationEs: V = 4 × 3 × 1.5 = 12 × 1.5 = 18 pulgadas cúbicas. Una arista fraccionaria no cambia los pasos.
hints: A fractional edge length works exactly like a whole-number one — the formula V = l × w × h does not change.
Multiply the two whole-number edges first, then multiply that product by the fractional height.
4 × 3 = 12. Now multiply 12 by 1½, which you can split into 12 × 1 plus 12 × ½.
hintsEs: Una arista fraccionaria funciona igual que una entera: la fórmula V = l × w × h no cambia.
Multiplica primero las dos aristas enteras y después multiplica ese producto por la altura fraccionaria.
4 × 3 = 12. Ahora multiplica 12 por 1½, que puedes separar en 12 × 1 más 12 × ½.

onLevel.title: Fix our table's thinking

workedExample.label: The problem
workedExample.work: How is volume different from area?
workedExample.workEs: ¿En qué se diferencia el volumen del área?

workedExample.label: A classmate at our table answered
workedExample.work: Volume uses square units; area uses cubic units
workedExample.labelEs: Un compañero de nuestra mesa respondió
workedExample.workEs: El volumen usa unidades cuadradas; el área usa unidades cúbicas

onLevel.correctWork: The correct answer is Volume measures 3D space (cubic units); area measures 2D surface (square units). Volume measures the space inside a 3D shape (cubic units like in³). Area measures a flat 2D surface (square units like in²).
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La respuesta correcta es El volumen mide el espacio en 3D (unidades cúbicas); el área mide una superficie en 2D (unidades cuadradas). El volumen mide el espacio dentro de una figura de tres dimensiones (unidades cúbicas como in³). El área mide una superficie plana de dos dimensiones (unidades cuadradas como in²).
hints: Think dimensions: area covers a flat 2D surface, while volume fills a 3D space.
hintsEs: Piensa en dimensiones: el área cubre una superficie plana 2D, mientras que el volumen llena un espacio 3D.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Volume of Rectangular Prisms is rounding a fractional edge length to the nearest whole number before multiplying, instead of using the exact fraction or decimal. For a box that is 2 ft × 1.5 ft × 1 ft, a student might round 1.5 down to 1 and compute 2 × 1 × 1 = 2 ft³, but the correct volume uses the exact edge length: 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 ft³ — a full cubic foot larger. Before you submit, ask: 'Did I multiply using the exact fractional or decimal edge length, or did I round it off first?'

diagram.title: Fish Tank Edge Lengths
diagram.caption: Read the three bars as the tank's length, width, and height, then multiply them: 24 × 12 × 16 = 4608 in³, which ÷ 231 ≈ 20 gallons.

connect.scenario: An aquarium store sells fish tanks. A small tank is 24 inches long, 12 inches wide, and 16 inches tall. One gallon of water takes up about 231 cubic inches.
connect.promptQuestion: How many gallons of water does the small tank hold?
connect.prompt: The tank's volume is ___ in³ because V = ___ × ___ × ___. It holds about ___ gallons because ___ ÷ 231 ≈ ___.

check.stem: About how many gallons does the tank hold?
Why divide by 231 instead of multiplying?
choices: Because you are finding how many 231-in³ gallons fit inside the tank
Because dividing always makes numbers smaller
Because gallons are bigger than inches
check.explanation: One gallon takes up 231 in³. Asking how many gallons fit in 4,608 in³ is asking how many groups of 231 fit — that is division.

connect.modelAnswer: V = 24 × 12 × 16 = 4,608 in³. One gallon is about 231 in³, so 4,608 ÷ 231 ≈ 19.9 — about 20 gallons.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: A rectangular prism has l = 7 ft, w = 2 ft, h = 3 ft. What is the volume?
exitTicket.explanation: V = 7 × 2 × 3 = 42 cubic feet. Remember: volume uses cubic units (ft³).
choiceFeedback: Not quite. V = 7 × 2 × 3 = ___ cubic feet.
Check the units. Area is square units (²), volume is cubic units (³).
Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
hints: Note the edges: l = 7 ft, w = 2 ft, h = 3 ft — and remember volume answers use cubic units (ft³).
Apply V = l × w × h, multiplying all three edges, and pick an answer with cubic units.
Multiply 7 × 2 = 14 first, then multiply that result by the height, 3 feet.
exitTicket.stemEs: Revisión rápida — tú puedes: Un prisma rectangular tiene l = 7 pies, a = 2 pies, h = 3 pies. ¿Cuál es el volumen?
exitTicket.explanationEs: V = 7 × 2 × 3 = 42 pies cúbicos. Recuerda: el volumen usa unidades cúbicas (pies³).
choiceFeedbackEs: Revisa las unidades. El área va en unidades cuadradas (²), el volumen en unidades cúbicas (³).
¿Estás sumando las dimensiones? El volumen multiplica todas las aristas: largo × ancho × altura.
hintsEs: Fíjate en las aristas: l = 7 pies, a = 2 pies, h = 3 pies — y recuerda que las respuestas de volumen usan unidades cúbicas (pies³).
Aplica V = l × a × h, multiplicando las tres aristas, y escoge una respuesta con unidades cúbicas.
Multiplica 7 × 2 = 14 primero, y luego multiplica ese resultado por la altura, 3 pies.

questions.stem: A regular hexagon splits into 6 identical triangles, each with an area of 8 square cm. What is the area of the hexagon?
questions.stemEs: Un hexágono regular se divide en 6 triángulos idénticos, cada uno con un área de 8 centímetros cuadrados. ¿Cuál es el área del hexágono?

questions.stem: A regular pentagon is decomposed into triangles from its centre. How many triangles are there?
questions.explanation: One triangle forms for each side, and a pentagon has 5 sides.
questions.stemEs: Un pentágono regular se descompone en triángulos desde su centro. ¿Cuántos triángulos hay?
questions.explanationEs: Se forma un triángulo por cada lado, y un pentágono tiene 5 lados.

questions.stem: A regular octagon has an area of 96 square inches and splits into 8 identical triangles. What is the area of one triangle?
questions.stemEs: Un octágono regular tiene un área de 96 pulgadas cuadradas y se divide en 8 triángulos idénticos. ¿Cuál es el área de un triángulo?

questions.stem: Why does decomposing a regular polygon into triangles help you find its area?
choices: Every triangle's area is easy to find, and the parts add to the whole
It turns the polygon into a rectangle
questions.explanation: You already know A = ½bh for a triangle, so you can find one piece and add up all the pieces.
questions.stemEs: ¿Por qué descomponer un polígono regular en triángulos te ayuda a hallar su área?
choicesEs: El área de cada triángulo es fácil de hallar, y las partes suman el entero
Convierte el polígono en un rectángulo
questions.explanationEs: Ya sabes que A = ½bh para un triángulo, así que puedes hallar una pieza y sumar todas las piezas.
